title: Stripe Funding and Valuation History (2010-2023)
content:
Stripe has raised a total of $8.7 billion across multiple funding rounds since its founding by Patrick and John Collison in 2010. The company initially received seed funding from Y Combinator, Peter Thiel, and Elon Musk. In its Series A round in 2011, Stripe raised $18 million led by Sequoia Capital. Its valuation rocketed over the years, reaching a peak of $95 billion in 2021 after a $600 million Series H round.

Most recently, in March 2023, Stripe announced a $6.5 billion Series I funding round at a significantly reduced valuation of $50 billion. The primary purpose of this massive round was not to fund operating costs, but to provide liquidity to current and former employees and address employee withholding tax obligations related to expiring restricted stock units (RSUs). The Series I round was backed by existing investors like Andreessen Horowitz, Baillie Gifford, Founders Fund, General Catalyst, MSD Partners, and Thrive Capital, along with new investors such as GIC, Goldman Sachs Asset and Wealth Management, and Temasek.
